classification.difficultyReason: Establish triangle similarity using parallel lines, then use the midpoint condition to prove a side-length relationship.

content.prompt: In the diagram, $AB=BC$ and $BM\parallel CN$. Prove that $CN=2BM$.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle ACN with B on AC and M on AN; BM joins B to M. Single ticks mark AB and BC equal, and matching arrows mark BM parallel to CN. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: A, B and C are collinear in that order; A, M and N are collinear in that order; AB=BC and BM is parallel to CN.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied geometry, labels and marks are visible.

answer.short:
$CN=2BM$.

$\triangle ABM\sim\triangle ACN$ (AAA), and $AC=2AB$, so corresponding sides give $CN=2BM$.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABM$ and $\triangle ACN$,

$\angle BAM=\angle CAN$ (same angle),

$\angle ABM=\angle ACN$ (corresponding angles, $BM\parallel CN$).

Therefore $\triangle ABM\sim\triangle ACN$ (AAA).

Since $AB=BC$,
$$\begin{align*}AC&=AB+BC\\AC&=2AB.\end{align*}$$
Matching sides of similar triangles give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{CN}{BM}&=\frac{AC}{AB}\\\frac{CN}{BM}&=\frac{2AB}{AB}\\\frac{CN}{BM}&=2\\CN&=2BM.\end{align*}$$
